Lessons.Title: Find Angle Measurements
ExplanationParagraphs: 2021 IM/KH G4 U07:L13 Find Angle Measurements. Goal: calculate unknown angle measures by adding or subtracting adjacent known angles; show angle size does NOT depend on length of drawn segments. Compose benchmark turns 90°, 180°, 360° with physical angle corners, tracing, measuring and folding. Archived local Our-CS source inspection reused.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: Notice and Wonder: Corner Pieces (10 minutes); Activity 1: How Big Are These Angles? (25 minutes); Activity 2: Angles in a Kite (10 minutes); Cool-down: Sets of Three Angles (5 minutes)

Mathematical rule: If two non-overlapping adjacent angles with a common vertex combine into a 90°, 180°, 360° or otherwise known turn, then unknown part = total degrees − known part. Illustrative independent examples: 90°−62°=28°; 180°−73°=107°. These particular numbers are Edulytics-authored, not verified publisher figure measurements.

Original Activity 1 How Big Are These Angles? (25 min): teacher gives materials to measure angles p,q,r,s relative to known right-angle components. The source student task requires explanation or actual display of reasoning; do not invent publisher p/q/r/s values from truncated text excerpts.

Original Activity 2 Angles in a Kite (10 min): take a SQUARE sheet and follow THREE original pictured folding steps to form a kite, then use fold-line and benchmark angles to reason. Real precise folds and the original kite diagrams are teacher-scored, not interpreted from source snippets.

First-party Edulytics Cool-down: a 180° straight angle includes one 73° adjacent part. The other is 180−73=107°. This is independently authored: original 2021 publisher Cool-down Sets of Three Angles is teacher-access gated.

Supplementary digital Practice extends the existing exact angle kernel with eight fixed first-party numerical adjacent-angle cases across right (90°), straight (180°), and full (360°) benchmark totals. Numerical accuracy does NOT establish whether a learner folded the source kite, measured source p,q,r,s, or reasoned from real cutouts.

KeyConcepts.Title: Additive adjacent angle measurement
KeyConcepts.Definition: Two adjacent nonoverlapping angles sharing a vertex together occupy the sum of their turn measures.
KeyConcepts.Rule: known + unknown = total; unknown = total - known.
KeyConcepts.Example: For a 90° right angle with a 62° part, the remaining angle is 28° (independent example).

KeyConcepts.Title: Turn benchmarks
KeyConcepts.Definition: A right angle has 90°, a straight angle 180°, and a full turn 360°.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Subtract components only within a specified total; check unknown is positive and both parts sum to the full turn.

KeyConcepts.Title: Segment length independence
KeyConcepts.Definition: The angular opening between rays does not depend on how long the drawn segments are.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Preserve ray directions and common vertex; longer/shorter segments alone do not change angle size.
KeyConcepts.Example: Two different-length rays with the same directions still form the same angle.

KeyConcepts.Title: Publisher source physical elements
KeyConcepts.Definition: Original p,q,r,s figures, corner pieces and square-to-kite folding require the original student images and physical materials.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Teacher checks original diagrams and constructions. First-party numeric problems are not copied source figures.
KeyConcepts.Example: Angles in a Kite is a 10-minute source activity with three pictured steps.

WorkedExamples.Title: First-party complement within a right angle
WorkedExamples.Question: A right angle 90° contains a 62° part. What is the other?
WorkedExamples.Method: Subtract a known adjacent part from total.

WorkedExamples.Title: First-party straight angle Cool-down
WorkedExamples.Question: A straight angle has a part measuring 73°. Find its remaining adjacent angle.

WorkedExamples.Title: First-party full-turn split
WorkedExamples.Question: Two non-overlapping adjacent turns total 360° and one measures 120°. What is the other?

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Adding when finding an unknown part of a known total.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The known part and unknown part must sum to the benchmark.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming longer rays make larger angles.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Only directions and shared vertex determine angular opening.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Compare the degree turn, not the drawn line lengths.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assigning 62° or 73° to the publisher's p,q,r,s or kite pictures.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Those figures were not visually measured here.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Treat these as Edulytics first-party numeric examples only.

SummaryPoints: Original source activities: Corner Pieces, p/q/r/s unknown angles, three-step square-to-kite physical folds.
Compose/decompose adjacent turns: unknown = total − known; benchmark totals 90°,180°,360°.
Changing ray length alone does not change angle measure.
First-party Cool-down 180°−73°=107° (not original gated publisher Cool-down).
